clue.text: Foreman at factory returning loose clothing

indicators.note: returning says the letters taken from the words are read backwards
loose here means the letters are set free from inside the run of words before it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A works foreman heads back to the factory in something loose and comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose clothing' reads as the definition, but the hidden-word step needs a signal, and only 'loose' is free: it lets NATFAC out of 'Foreman at factory', and 'returning' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A kaftan is a long tunic, a garment and so an item of clothing.

clue.text: Break into car at Alpine resort

indicators.note: break signals the following letters are smashed up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A thief breaks into a car parked at a ski resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'car' looks like the definition but is fodder: 'Break' rearranges INTO CAR. The Cortina was also a Ford car.
explanation.definitionFit: Cortina d'Ampezzo is a ski town in the Italian Dolomites, an Alpine resort.

clue.text: Concentrate on diplomats America caught hacking

indicators.note: hacking means breaking into, so this letter cuts into the other pieces

parts.note: FO is the Foreign Office, the UK's diplomatic service
US stands for the United States
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An instruction to concentrate on diplomats America has caught hacking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hacking' puts C (caught) into FO US; the Foreign Office is the UK's diplomatic ministry.
explanation.definitionFit: To focus is to direct one's attention, a synonym verb for concentrate.

indicators.note: beneath in a down clue places the tool's letters below the others

parts.note: a vice is a clamping tool, so clamp

explanation.surface: Wickedness lurking under a river crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vice' looks moral but is the workshop tool, a clamp.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc lamp produces brilliant illumination from an electric arc, so it is a type of lamp.

parts.note: a gala is a festive party or celebration
the x and y axes of a graph give the letters X and Y

explanation.surface: A rowdy party where axes are swung, with celebrities on hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'axes' is not tools but the two axes of a graph, x and y.
explanation.definitionFit: A galaxy is a vast system holding billions of stars, so stars are found there.

indicators.note: moulting wings means shedding the outer letters of each word

explanation.surface: A small bird in a panic as its wings moult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moulting wings' strips the ends off PANIC and SMALL, leaving ANI and MAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal is any living beast, a synonym for creature.

clue.text: Heavy metal group to perform mid-month?

parts.note: to act is to perform on stage
in the Ides, the middle day of a Roman month

explanation.surface: A heavy metal band scheduled to play a gig in the middle of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ides were the 13th or 15th day of the Roman month, so mid-month is IN IDES.
explanation.definitionFit: The actinides are a series of heavy radioactive elements in the periodic table, a group of metals.

indicators.note: flipping turns the whole run of letters over

parts.note: egad is an old-fashioned exclamation of surprise
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Someone marvels at the size of an old flipping fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' reverses EGAD RAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardage is distance measured in yards, a length.

clue.text: Repeatedly cross river to welcome Raging Bull writer

indicators.note: to welcome means the doubled word takes the other letters in
repeatedly calls for the crossing word to appear twice

parts.note: to ford a river is to cross it
raging is mad and a bull is an ox

explanation.surface: A writer of the film Raging Bull keeps crossing a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raging Bull' is a boxing film, but here it is MAD OX, welcomed between two FORDs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ford Madox Ford was an English novelist, author of The Good Soldier.

clue.text: We leave a plant for a reptile

indicators.note: leave tells us those letters depart from the word for the plant

parts.note: the crocus is a spring-flowering plant
we is replaced by its object form us, the same people

explanation.surface: Gardeners abandon a plant and take up keeping a reptile instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' takes US (we) out of CROCUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Croc is the everyday short form of crocodile, a large reptile.

indicators.note: around signals the letters of the following words are moved about

explanation.surface: A church choir gathers about its cross to sing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks positional but asks for the letters of THEIR CROSS to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a choir are the people whose job is to sing in it.

clue.text: Holiday at new site, wearing absolutely nothing

indicators.note: wearing means the outer letters are put on around the inner ones like clothes

parts.note: FA is short for Fanny Adams, British slang for nothing at all

indicators.note: new signals the word site is made over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Naturists on holiday at a new campsite wear nothing whatsoever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the word site and 'wearing' sets it inside FA, from 'sweet Fanny Adams', British slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a religious festival day in Spanish-speaking countries, a public holiday.

clue.text: Pinched a bit of corn on approach

parts.note: a pinched face is drawn, thin and strained
an ear is the seed-bearing head of a cereal plant

explanation.surface: Someone stole a little corn while on approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinched' suggests stealing, but it means looking strained and thin.
explanation.definitionFit: To come close to something is to near it; the phrase is a verb synonym for come closer.

clue.text: Frenchman left au pairs inside playing possum?

indicators.note: inside says the shuffled words go within the other two letters

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a French gentleman

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are frolicking into a new order

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's departing au pairs are inside, pretending to be asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing possum' means feigning death; here 'playing' rearranges AU PAIRS into ARSUPIA, set inside M and L. The question mark marks the possum as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The possum carries its young in a pouch, making it one example of a pouched mammal.

clue.text: Ken exits wounded, holding up TV award, though showing good balance

indicators.note: holding means the shortened word contains the reversed award
exits means the name leaves the word for wounded

parts.note: stricken means struck down or wounded
a man's name taken as written

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the award is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Emmy is the US television award

explanation.surface: Ken leaves hurt yet holds his TV award up with perfect poise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exits' takes KEN from STRICKEN, leaving STRIC, which holds YMME ('up' on EMMY).
explanation.definitionFit: Having matching halves means being evenly proportioned, which is good balance.

indicators.note: off means these letters are taken away from the word for the book

parts.note: a ledger is an account book
the left and right hands give L and R

explanation.surface: Instructions to inch forward with your hands off the book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes L and R (left and right hands) from LEDGER.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch forward cautiously is to edge along, a synonym verb.

parts.note: bum is British slang for the backside

indicators.note: leading picks out the head letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A runner jogs along behind the leading professional athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' is a noun here, BUM (British slang for backside).
explanation.definitionFit: To jog someone is to knock or nudge them, which is a synonym for a jolt or knock.

definitions.meaning: the home of a colony's queen bee
a tall, domed hairdo popular in the 1960s

explanation.surface: The monarch lives in grand style.
explanation.definitionFit: The bee colony's home holds its queen, and the hairdo is named after its domed shape.

clue.text: Mobile homes — a lot are horrible

indicators.note: mobile means the letters are free to move into a new order

explanation.surface: A sniffy verdict that most mobile homes are ghastly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile' rearranges HOMES and A LOT together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something loathsome causes disgust, making it hateful or repulsive.

indicators.note: carrying means the outer word bears the poles within it

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic property
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Workers cross a site carrying long poles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'property' is a quality, not land.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is passage across or through a place, a crossing.

indicators.note: mounting in a down clue means the letters climb, read upwards

parts.note: a gnat is a small fly
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: The horsefly is becoming a growing problem.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition hides in the front of 'Horsefly', which splits so that its tail, 'fly', starts the wordplay; 'mounting' reverses the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A mustang is a feral horse of the American West.

clue.text: Cat given joint with Italian sauce over

parts.note: co- is a prefix meaning joint, as in co-owner

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the sauce is turned upside down

parts.note: ragu is an Italian meat sauce

explanation.surface: A cat served a joint of meat with Italian sauce poured over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' looks like meat but is the prefix CO; 'over' reverses RAGU.
explanation.definitionFit: The cougar, or puma, is a large American wild cat.

clue.text: Fantastic being with us on westbound jet

parts.note: us gives the subject form we, the same group
re means on or about, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: westbound in an across clue means read from right to left

parts.note: a jet of liquid is a flow

explanation.surface: A fabulous creature joins us aboard a jet heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'westbound' reads the jet's word from right to left; 'on' is RE, as in a letter heading.
explanation.definitionFit: A werewolf is a creature of fantasy and folklore, a monster that is not real.

indicators.note: in places the picked letters inside the word for brilliant

parts.note: ace means excellent or brilliant

indicators.note: odd picks out the first, third and fifth letters of the following word

explanation.surface: Praise for a brilliant book full of strange clues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' gives CUS from CLUES, which goes 'in' ACE; 'book' is the police verb, not a volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Police book a suspect when they formally charge them, which is to accuse them.

indicators.note: shedding means losing the stated part

parts.note: Capricorn is the goat sign of the zodiac
a corn is a patch of hard skin on the foot

explanation.surface: An island goat moults its tough hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shedding' removes CORN from CAPRICORN.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an Italian island in the Bay of Naples.

parts.note: to dis someone is slang for insulting or putting them down
regards is a letter sign-off like best wishes

explanation.surface: Someone forgets to sign off a letter with best wishes.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore or pay no attention to something is to neglect it.

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: to consume food is to eat it

explanation.surface: Pensioners take priority when burning up the fuel supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried turf from bogs is burnt for heating, a traditional fuel.

indicators.note: bridges means the outer letters span across the inner ones

parts.note: est is the abbreviation for established, as on shop signs
cor is a British exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: An exclamation of wonder at a shepherd's sturdy old bridges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridges' is a verb: EST spans COR, a British cry of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: To shepherd people is to guide or accompany them, a synonym verb.

indicators.note: lost means the letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: staring is looking fixedly

explanation.surface: A viewer glued to a television series they have lost track of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' drops A from STARING.
explanation.definitionFit: A string of events or wins is a run or sequence, the same idea as a series.
